AnsiEntry.description:
Text whose SGR escape sequences (`ESC [ … m`) set its colours and
attributes, drawn cell by cell: the output of a command run with its
colours, or a mockup of a terminal screen. Named colours follow the
terminal's theme. Every other escape sequence is dropped. Exactly one of
`path` and `content` is given.

content.description:
The text itself, in place of a file. JSON writes the escape
character as `\u001b`.

path.description:
An absolute path to the file to show; `asqr ask` makes a relative
one absolute.

title.description: A name for the entry, such as a file name.

Choice.description: One option of a `single` or `multi` question.

context.description:
Shown in place of the question's context while the cursor is on
this option, so the person can compare options before picking.

description.description:
Shown in full and wrapped, however long it is. Markdown: a single
newline breaks the line, and raw HTML shows as written.

label.description:
The short handle the person picks the option by, shown in full and
wrapped. Markdown: a single newline breaks the line, and raw HTML
shows as written. Longer text goes into `description`, or into
`context`.

CodeEntry.description:
Text shown exactly as written and highlighted, like a fenced code
block: source code, a log, terminal output, a configuration file, or
the source of a Markdown file. Exactly one of `path` and `content` is
given.

content.description: The text itself, in place of a file.

language.description:
The language for highlighting, such as `rust` or `json`. Without
it, the extension of `path`, then of `title`, decides.

path.description:
An absolute path to the file to show; `asqr ask` makes a relative
one absolute.

title.description:
A name for the entry, such as a file name. Its extension picks the
language when neither `language` nor `path` does.

ContextEntry.description: One entry of a `context` list. The `type` field picks the kind.

Custom.description: The `custom` field: either a plain switch or a configured entry.

DiffEntry.description:
A change between two versions of a text, which asqr diffs itself. A
missing `old` is a new file, a missing `new` a deleted one.

language.description:
The language for highlighting the unchanged lines, such as `rust`
or `tsx`. Without it, the extension of `name` decides.

name.description:
The file name the diff is about, shown in the header. Its extension
picks the language when `language` does not.

title.description: A name for the entry, such as a file name.

DiffSide.description:
One side of a diff: a file or inline content. Exactly one of the two
is given.

content.description: The text itself, in place of a file.

path.description: An absolute path; `asqr ask` makes a relative one absolute.

ImageEntry.description:
An image file. PNG, JPEG, GIF (first frame only), WebP, BMP, TIFF,
ICO, TGA, PNM, QOI, DDS, OpenEXR, HDR and farbfeld are shown. SVG and
AVIF are not.

enlarge.description:
`false` keeps the image at its natural size where it fits, instead
of scaling it up to fill the space it gets. A larger image still
shrinks to fit.

path.description: An absolute path; `asqr ask` makes a relative one absolute.

title.description: A name for the entry, such as a file name.

oneOf.description:
Shows its text and context and takes no answer; the person may add
a note.

Length.description:
How long typed text should be (spec section 7.7). Both parts are
optional; validation checks that they are consistent. There is no hard
limit: the counter guides, and input is never refused (ADR 8).

target.description: The range the text should land in.

warn.description: Above this the counter warns more strongly.

MarkdownEntry.description:
Markdown, rendered and wrapped to the space it gets. Exactly one of
`path` and `content` is given.

content.description: The Markdown itself, in place of a file.

path.description:
An absolute path to the file to show; `asqr ask` makes a relative
one absolute.

title.description: A name for the entry, such as a file name.

Question.description:
One item of the session: a thing for the person to decide, or, of kind
`info`, something to read.

context.description:
Material shown next to the question that helps to answer it. Most
questions have none. A list, of which this asqr shows one entry.

custom.description: Whether a typed answer is allowed next to the options.

header.description: A short label for the question list; the id is shown without it.

length.description:
Length limits of the answer of a `text` question. A custom entry
carries its own limits inside `custom`.

min.description: Bounds on the number of selected options of a `multi` question.

note.description:
Ignored: every question and info item takes a note. A file that sets
it stays valid.

options.description: The choices of a `single` or `multi` question.

text.description:
The question, or what an info item shows. Markdown: a single
newline breaks the line, and raw HTML shows as written.

description: One session: a list of questions answered and submitted as a whole.

asqr.description: The format version. Only `2` is supported.

follows.description: The id of an earlier session this one continues (spec section 3.1).

from.description: Who is asking, shown in the session header.

id.description:
The session id. Optional, because `asqr ask` assigns a ULID when it
is missing and a hand-dropped file takes its file stem as the id.

intro.description:
Markdown, shown under the title in at most two lines. A single
newline breaks the line, and raw HTML shows as written.

title: Session
